options_english.C: For maximum utilization of available water resources.

questions.text: (क) पर्यावरणीय निश्चयवाद की संकल्पना की उदाहरण सहित व्याख्या कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: (A) Explain the concept of environmental determinism with examples.
questions.instruction_line: अथवा (ख) प्रकृति और मानव के बीच द्वैतता वैध नहीं है । इस कथन की उदाहरण सहित व्याख्या कीजिए ।
questions.instruction_line_english: OR (B) The dichotomy between nature and human is not valid. Explain this statement with examples.

key_points: Examples: Primitive societies living in harmony with nature

questions.solution: Environmental determinism posits that the physical environment, rather than social conditions, determines culture and human activities. In the early stages of human civilization, humans were highly dependent on their natural environment for food, shelter, and survival, making them passive agents of nature. However, with technological progress, humans have learned to modify their environment to suit their needs, showing that the stark dichotomy between nature and human is no longer strictly valid as they exist in a continuous interaction.

questions.text: भारत में ग्रामीण-नगरीय जनसंख्या के संगठन की मुख्य विशेषताओं का विश्लेषण कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Analyze the main characteristics of the rural-urban population composition in India.

key_points: Majority of population lives in rural areas
Difference in socio-economic and employment structures

questions.solution: The rural-urban composition in India shows a dominance of the rural population, with a vast majority still living in villages. However, there is a steady trend towards urbanization due to migration. Rural areas are largely engaged in primary activities like agriculture, while urban areas have diverse economies with concentrations in secondary and tertiary sectors, higher literacy rates, and better infrastructure compared to the rural hinterland.

questions.text: (क) विश्व व्यापार संगठन की होने वाली आलोचनाओं की व्याख्या कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: (A) Explain the criticisms directed towards the World Trade Organisation (WTO).
questions.instruction_line: अथवा (ख) व्यापार संतुलन क्या है ? व्यापार संतुलन की विशेषताओं की व्याख्या कीजिए ।
questions.instruction_line_english: OR (B) What is Balance of Trade? Explain the characteristics of Balance of Trade.

key_points: WTO Criticisms: Favours developed nations, ignores environmental/labour standards, affects sovereignty
Balance of Trade: Difference between value of imports and exports, Surplus vs Deficit

questions.solution: The World Trade Organisation (WTO) is often criticized for allegedly favoring the interests of developed nations over developing ones. Critics argue that its policies regarding intellectual property and trade liberalization undermine national sovereignty and may overlook environmental and labour standards. Alternatively, the Balance of Trade is defined as the difference between the monetary value of a country's imports and exports over a certain period. A balance of trade surplus occurs when exports exceed imports, while a deficit occurs when imports exceed exports, which significantly impacts a nation's economic health.

questions.text: भारत में नगरीय अपशिष्ट निस्तारण की समस्या के समाधान के लिए किन्हीं तीन उपायों की व्याख्या कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Explain any three measures to solve the problem of urban waste disposal in India.
questions.solution: Three key measures to address urban waste disposal in India are: First, mandatory segregation of waste at the source (household/commercial) into biodegradable and non-biodegradable components. Second, promoting recycling and composting facilities to reduce the volume of waste going to landfills. Third, strengthening public infrastructure for waste collection and raising awareness among citizens about responsible waste management practices.

questions.text: मानव विकास के मुख्य उद्देश्य के लिए विकल्पों की स्वतंत्रता पर बल देने वाले अर्थशास्त्री का नाम लिखिए । मानव विकास के चार स्तंभों की व्याख्या कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Write the name of the economist who emphasized freedom of choices for the main objective of Human Development. Explain the four pillars of Human Development.

key_points: Four pillars: Equity, Sustainability, Productivity, Empowerment

questions.solution: The economist who emphasized the freedom of choice as the main objective of Human Development is Dr. Mahbub-ul-Haq. The four pillars of Human Development are Equity, Sustainability, Productivity, and Empowerment. Equity refers to ensuring equal access to opportunities for all individuals, regardless of gender, race, or income. Sustainability means ensuring continuity in the availability of opportunities for future generations. Productivity involves investing in human resources to increase their capability and efficiency, while Empowerment refers to the ability of individuals to make their own choices by gaining increased freedom and capability.

questions.text: (क) भूमध्य सागर-हिंद महासागर मार्ग का नाम लिखिए । इसकी प्रमुख विशेषताओं की व्याख्या कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: (A) Name the Mediterranean Sea-Indian Ocean sea route. Explain its major characteristics.

key_points: Characteristics: Connects Europe and Asia, shortens distance, highly busy, strategic importance

questions.solution: The Mediterranean Sea-Indian Ocean sea route is primarily facilitated by the Suez Canal. Its major characteristics include significantly shortening the travel distance between European ports and Asian markets compared to the route around the Cape of Good Hope. It is one of the world's busiest shipping lanes, facilitating massive volumes of global trade, including oil, manufactured goods, and raw materials, making it a vital strategic point for international maritime commerce.

questions.text: भारत में वर्षा जल संग्रहण की आवश्यकता और इसके लाभों की व्याख्या कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Explain the need for and benefits of rainwater harvesting in India.

key_points: Need: Depleting groundwater, seasonal rainfall, water scarcity
Benefits: Recharge groundwater, reduce runoff, drought mitigation, sustainable water supply

questions.solution: Rainwater harvesting is essential in India due to the country's reliance on seasonal monsoons and the rapid depletion of groundwater resources across many states. The benefits of rainwater harvesting include recharging underground aquifers, which stabilizes the water table. It also reduces surface runoff, thereby minimizing soil erosion and preventing urban flooding during heavy rains. Furthermore, it provides a sustainable, cost-effective source of water for irrigation and household needs, acting as a vital buffer against drought in semi-arid and water-scarce regions.

questions.text: भारत में लोहा और इस्पात उद्योग के विकास को प्रभावित करने वाले कारकों का विश्लेषण कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Analyze the factors affecting the development of the iron and steel industry in India.
questions.solution: The development of India's iron and steel industry is influenced by several critical factors. The most important is the availability of essential raw materials like high-grade iron ore and coking coal, which determines plant location, usually in the Chota Nagpur plateau region. Efficient transport networks, including railways and ports, are necessary to move heavy materials. Growing domestic and international market demand drives production. Finally, state support through industrial policies, as well as access to capital and advanced manufacturing technology, are essential for maintaining competitiveness and sustainable growth.

questions.text_english: Describe the spatial distribution of population density in India.

key_points: Very high density in Indo-Gangetic plains
Moderate in coastal regions and peninsular India
Low in arid, mountainous, and forested regions
Influenced by climate, topography, and agriculture

questions.solution: The spatial distribution of population density in India is highly uneven due to various geographical and economic factors. The Indo-Gangetic plains, including states like Bihar and West Bengal, exhibit very high population density due to fertile alluvial soil, flat terrain, and abundant water, which support intensive agriculture. Coastal regions also show moderate to high density. Conversely, the arid regions of Rajasthan, the mountainous regions of the Himalayas, and the heavily forested tracts of central India show low population density because of harsh terrain, extreme climate, or poor accessibility, which limit economic opportunities.
